solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stalwart keeps returning as celebrity children's TV character

indicators.note: a word that keeps something holds it within, so the stalwart word goes round the rest

parts.note: stalwart means firm, steadfast

indicators.note: returning means the words as and celebrity are read backwards together

parts.note: a celebrity is a name, as in 'a big name'

explanation.surface: A dependable star turns up again as a famous figure on children's television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses both words together, giving EMANSA, and 'keeps' sets that inside the stalwart word. 'Stalwart' looks like a noun for a loyal person; here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireman Sam is the title hero of a long-running British animated series for small children about a Welsh firefighter.

clue.text: One used to snap and be tearful, upset by urgent news

parts.note: a news flash is an urgent bulletin

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word over, so it is read upwards

parts.note: to blub is to cry

explanation.surface: Someone liable to snap and cry, thrown by an urgent bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BLUB into BULB beneath FLASH. 'snap' suggests losing one's temper; it means taking a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashbulb is the single-use bulb once fired to light a photograph, a snap.

clue.text: Lecture man on sex — husband

parts.note: re means on or concerning
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A man giving a talk about sex to a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reith Lectures are annual BBC radio lectures named after Lord Reith, the BBC's first director-general.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Reith is the man whose name the BBC's Reith Lectures carry.

clue.text: Merchant at first devious has to promise to give change

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the trader word is taken
devious means winding or crooked, so the following letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crafty trader must make a pledge in order to hand over some coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges HAS TO PROMISE. 'change' looks like coins in the surface; it is a transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: A metamorphosis is a transformation, as from caterpillar to butterfly.

clue.text: Solution that's popular and in no way peculiar

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
rum is British slang for odd, peculiar

explanation.surface: A remedy that is popular and not at all odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet remedy or cure-all, a favoured fix of doubtful worth.

clue.text: White loaf to stop a short period of fasting

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so the idling word fills the middle
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
to loaf or bum around is to idle

explanation.surface: Bread used to break a brief fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the fasting period to LEN, and 'to stop' plugs it with the idling word. 'loaf' looks like bread; it is the verb meaning to idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg.

clue.text: Paper copy

definitions.meaning: the ... is a newspaper title, such as the Liverpool ...

explanation.definitionFit: Many local newspapers are called the Echo, and to echo someone is to imitate them.

clue.text: Reasons copper's got to arrest E European dictator

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the single letter is held inside the reasons word

parts.note: causes are reasons
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman has grounds to detain an Eastern European tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman; it is the metal. E stands as given.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolae Ceausescu was the communist dictator of Romania until 1989.

clue.text: Odd or even excerpts from voluntaries

indicators.note: even excerpts are the letters in even positions, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Organ pieces sampled for odd or even bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd or even' reads like a pair of choices; 'Odd' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional or bizarre, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Peers having come up briefly returned drunk

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to come up is to arise

indicators.note: returned means the word for a drunk is read backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: Lords who have risen to the top come back home tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims ARISE to ARIS; 'returned' turns SOT into TOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristos is informal shortening of aristocrats, and peers of the realm are the aristocracy.

clue.text: Second rate, poor Aston Villa, losing 5-1 on aggregate

parts.note: B is a second-rate grade, after A

indicators.note: poor suggests the football club's letters are in a bad, disordered state
losing says the betting odds are taken out of the club's name before rearranging

parts.note: 5-1 on is a betting price, written V (5) I (1) ON

explanation.surface: A mediocre football team, Aston Villa, goes down 5-1 over two legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes V, I and ON from ASTON VILLA, leaving ASTLLA, which 'poor' rearranges to ALLAST. 'on aggregate' looks like football scoring; 'aggregate' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is crushed stone or gravel, and aggregate is the builders' word for such broken stone.

clue.text: See about register for US arts venue

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Lincoln is one
c. (circa) means about
to enter is to record or register

explanation.surface: Check on enrolment for an American arts centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln Center is New York's performing arts complex, home to the Met Opera.

clue.text: Flat has garden — we hear sound of bees

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to garden can mean to hoe
bees make a hum

explanation.surface: An apartment with a garden, where the buzzing of bees can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, HOE gives HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum describes something dull or boring, and a flat performance is lifeless in the same way.

clue.text: Look back and note source, one that is retained

parts.note: re is a note in the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: retained means kept within, so the source word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a mine is a source of supply, as in a mine of information
I is the Roman numeral one
sc. (scilicet) is Latin shorthand for that is, namely

explanation.surface: An instruction to review and record where something came from, including one item that was kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retained' places I and the abbreviation for scilicet inside the source word. That Latin shorthand for 'that is' is less familiar than i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall the past with pleasure, which is looking back in memory.

clue.text: Lacking politeness, if innocuous — merely unsettling

indicators.note: unsettling disturbs the two words before it, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rudeness, even when harmless, can still be disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettling' rearranges INNOCUOUS and MERELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unceremoniously means doing it abruptly, without courtesy or due formality.

clue.text: Fred wrangling with Colin: I'm all ears!

definitions.note: the answer speaks for itself: a field full of ears of corn

indicators.note: wrangling is arguing and tussling, so the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly listening to two men argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrangling' jumbles FRED and COLIN. 'I'm all ears!' is the definition, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornfield is full of ears of corn, so it could say it is all ears.

clue.text: I agree twice to cross the road, horse having gone past

indicators.note: to cross is to span, so the agreement words lie either side of the rest

parts.note: yes and ay are two ways of saying I agree

indicators.note: having gone means the horse letter leaves

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, horse

explanation.surface: Agreeing twice to cross the road after a horse has gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone' drops heroin's H from 'the' plus the road abbreviation, leaving TERD; 'to cross' spans it with the two agreements. 'horse' is drug slang, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday can mean the past in general, as in 'yesterday's men'.

clue.text: Whereby some are entitled to celebrate the arrival of the monarch

definitions.text: Whereby some are entitled to celebrate the arrival of the monarch

parts.words: Whereby some are entitled to celebrate the arrival of the monarch
parts.note: 'entitled' means given titles such as knighthoods, and 'arrival of the monarch' is the sovereign's birth, celebrated each year

explanation.definitionFit: The Birthday Honours are the British honours list published on the monarch's official birthday, awarding knighthoods and other titles.

clue.text: Lead Civil Engineer, after promotion, getting rise

indicators.note: after says the lead and engineer pieces follow the promotion piece

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion
the van is the lead, the front of an army

explanation.surface: A senior civil engineer gets a pay rise after being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' suggests a job move; it is an ad.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is a rise, as in an advance in prices.

clue.text: Demanding toy car

parts.note: hard means demanding or difficult
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: A tricky toy car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof.

clue.text: Delivery agent returned earthenware vase, filling bottles

indicators.note: returned means the concealed letters are read backwards
bottles means holds inside, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: A courier sends back a pottery vase, while packing bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' holds REVASEFIL inside 'earthenware vase, filling'; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifesaver rescues people, and to deliver is to rescue or set free, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Commentator's to favour one side's scorer

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so the answer is the word as heard

parts.note: to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A pundit says a sports scorer favours one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests a sports scorer; it means someone who writes scores of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer, who wrote musical scores.

clue.text: Ecstasy, see, when one's out for a duck

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: one is out and replaced by a, so the letter is swapped

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Drugs, look, when a batsman is dismissed without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: In VIDE, I is swapped for A, giving VADE. In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge or avoid it.

clue.text: Girl that's lifted bible getting into trouble

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the bible letters sit inside the trouble word

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised, read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A girl who stole a bible ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns RV to VR, which goes into AIL. 'lifted' suggests stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Avril is a girl's name, French for April.

clue.text: Don't strike boy in hat

parts.note: stet is a proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, don't strike out
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A plea not to hit a lad wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, named after its maker.

clue.text: Did coach express disapproval? Nothing radical

parts.note: to tut is to express disapproval
O is zero, nothing
red is slang for a radical left-winger

explanation.surface: Was the trainer cross? Nothing extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to teach privately, which is what a coach does.

clue.text: Flap in one's in-tray

definitions.meaning: a flap is a fuss, a commotion
work waiting in one's in-tray is still ...

explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, and tasks still waiting to be done are on one's to-do pile.

clue.text: In time, what's taken to get one open-mouthed?

parts.note: the temp, short for temperature, is what a nurse takes
orally means by mouth, needing it open

explanation.surface: A question about how a temperature reading is taken: by mouth, with the thermometer under the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporally means relating to time, as opposed to space.
